blocks.text: Mehmonga choy taklif qilganda o'zbekchada «Choy ichasizmi?», «Choy quyaymi?» deymiz, do'konda esa «Bir kilo olma bering» yoki «...olmoqchi edim» deymiz. Ingliz tilida bunday xushmuomala taklif va iltimoslar uchun **would like** ishlatiladi. **Would you like** ...? — taklif: «...ni xohlaysizmi?». **I'd like** ... (= I **would** like) — xushmuomala istak: «...ni xohlardim», «...olmoqchi edim». Ma'nosi **want** ga yaqin, lekin ancha muloyim eshitiladi.

**would like** dan keyin ikki xil narsa keladi. Ot: **Would you like** some tea? — «Choy ichasizmi?». Yoki fe'l — bu holda `to` **shart**: **Would you like to** come? — «Kelasizmi?». Modal fe'llardan farqli ravishda (can go, must go), bu yerda **like to go** bo'ladi. Qisqa shakllar: I**'d**, you**'d**, he**'d**, she**'d**, we**'d**, they**'d** = I **would** ...

items.text: **Would you like to** watch a film tonight?
Lola **would like** a new phone for her birthday.

blocks.text: Do'konda, kafeda, mehmonxonada nimadir so'raganda **I'd like** ... eng qulay shakl: **I'd like** a single room, please. «I want ...» grammatik jihatdan to'g'ri, lekin begona odamga qo'pol eshitilishi mumkin — xuddi o'zbekchada «Menga xona kerak!» deb buyurgandek. **I'd like to** ... — «...moqchi edim», «...ni xohlardim»: **I'd like to** speak to the manager. Orzu va rejalar ham shunday aytiladi: One day **I'd like to** see Paris.

items.text: **I'd like** a single room for two nights, please.
items.translation: Ikki kechaga bir kishilik xona **olmoqchi edim**.

items.text: We**'d like to** pay now, please.

blocks.text: Do you like ...? yoki Would you like ...?

Bu ikki savol bir-biriga o'xshaydi, lekin ma'nosi boshqa. **Do you like** ...? — umuman, doim yoqadimi: «...ni yaxshi ko'rasizmi?» (Present Simple, → 7-dars). **Would you like** ...? — hozir, aniq bir taklif: «...ni xohlaysizmi?». Xuddi shunday **I like** tea — «Choyni yaxshi ko'raman», **I'd like** tea — «Choy ichsam bo'lardi (hozir)». O'zbek o'quvchisi ko'pincha shu yerda adashadi.

items.text: **Do you like** green tea? — Yes, I drink it every day.
items.translation: Ko'k choyni **yaxshi ko'rasizmi**? — Ha, har kuni ichaman.

items.text: **Would you like** green tea or black? — Green, please.
items.translation: Ko'k choy **ichasizmi** yoki qora? — Ko'k, iltimos.

blocks.text: Javoblar: Yes, please / No, thank you

Taklifga eng tabiiy javoblar: **Yes, please.** — «Ha, iltimos» va **No, thank you.** / **No, thanks.** — «Yo'q, rahmat». Taklifni mamnuniyat bilan qabul qilish: **I'd love to.** — «Bajonidil», «Juda xohlardim». Muloyim rad etish: **I'd love to, but** I'm busy. — «Juda xohlardim-u, lekin bandman». «Yes, I like» yoki «Yes, I would like» deyish g'alati eshitiladi.

So'roq so'zlar bilan: **What would you like?** — «Nima olasiz?», **Where would you like to go?** — «Qayerga borishni xohlaysiz?». Boshqa odamdan biror ish so'rash (I'd like you to ..., Would you like me to ...?) — 53-darsda.

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «Would you like coming?» → **Would you like to come?**; «I would like go.» → **I'd like to go.** (`to` shart); «Do you like a cup of tea?» (taklif qilganda) → **Would you like a cup of tea?**; «I like a coffee, please.» (kafeda) → **I'd like a coffee, please.**; «Would you like tea? — Yes, I like.» → **Yes, please.**

Eslab qolish: «...ichasizmi?», «...olasizmi?», «...kelasizmi?» deb taklif qilsangiz — **Would you like** ...?; «...olmoqchi edim», «...xohlardim» — **I'd like** .... Fe'l kelsa — `to` ni unutmang: like **to** come.

examples.title: Offers: **Would you like** + noun?
examples.description: Taklif: **Would you like** + ot? = «...ichasizmi?», «...olasizmi?», «...beraymi?». Javob: Yes, please. / No, thank you.

sentences.text: **Would you like** a cup of tea?
sentences.translation: Bir piyola choy **ichasizmi**?

sentences.text: Aziz, **would you like** some more plov? — Yes, please. It's delicious.
sentences.translation: Aziz, yana palov **olasanmi**? — Ha, iltimos. Juda mazali.

sentences.text: Excuse me, **would you like** a newspaper? — No, thank you.
sentences.translation: Kechirasiz, gazeta **xohlaysizmi**? — Yo'q, rahmat.

sentences.text: It's cold in here. **Would you like** a blanket?
sentences.translation: Bu yer sovuq ekan. Adyol **olib kelaymi**?

sentences.text: Mrs Brown, **would you like** a seat? You can sit here.
sentences.translation: Missis Braun, **o'tirasizmi**? Mana shu yerga o'tiring.

sentences.text: **Would you like** milk in your coffee?
sentences.translation: Qahvangizga sut **qo'shaymi**?

sentences.text: Dilnoza, **would you like** an apple or a banana?
sentences.translation: Dilnoza, olma **xohlaysanmi** yoki banan?

sentences.text: You look thirsty. **Would you like** a glass of cold water?
sentences.translation: Chanqaganga o'xshaysiz. Bir stakan sovuq suv **ichasizmi**?

sentences.text: Before you go, **would you like** a piece of cake to take home?
sentences.translation: Ketishdan oldin uyga bir bo'lak tort **olib ketasizmi**?

sentences.text: We've got some fresh bread from the market. **Would** your children **like** some?
sentences.translation: Bozordan yangi non olib keldik. Bolalaringizga **beraylikmi**?

examples.title: Invitations: **Would you like to** ...?
examples.description: Biror ishga chaqirish: **Would you like to** + fe'l? = «...asizmi?», «...ishni xohlaysizmi?». Fe'ldan oldin `to` shart.

sentences.text: **Would you like to** come to dinner on Saturday?
sentences.translation: Shanba kuni kechki ovqatga **kelasizmi**?

sentences.text: Madina, **would you like to** dance?
sentences.translation: Madina, **raqsga tushasanmi**?

sentences.text: We're going to the cinema tonight. **Would you like to** join us?
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun kinoga boryapmiz. Bizga **qo'shilasizmi**?

sentences.text: **Would** your parents **like to** visit Samarkand with us next month?
sentences.translation: Ota-onangiz kelasi oy biz bilan Samarqandga **borishni xohlaydilarmi**?

sentences.text: Tom, **would you like to** play tennis after work?
sentences.translation: Tom, ishdan keyin tennis **o'ynaysanmi**?

sentences.text: Our friends are coming on Friday. **Would** Sarah **like to** come too?
sentences.translation: Juma kuni do'stlarimiz kelishyapti. Sara ham **kelishni xohlaydimi**?

sentences.text: It's a lovely evening. **Would you like to** go for a walk?
sentences.translation: Ajoyib oqshom. **Sayrga chiqamizmi**?

sentences.text: Bekzod, **would you like to** try driving my car?
sentences.translation: Bekzod, mashinamni **haydab ko'rasanmi**?

sentences.text: Hello, this is Emma. **Would you like to** meet for coffee tomorrow?
sentences.translation: Salom, bu Emma. Ertaga qahva ichgani **uchrashamizmi**?

sentences.text: Guess what? Our photos from Bukhara are ready. **Would you like to** see them?
sentences.translation: Bilasizmi? Buxorodagi suratlarimiz tayyor. **Ko'rishni xohlaysizmi**?

examples.title: **I'd like** ...: in shops and cafés
examples.description: Do'kon, kafe, kassada xushmuomala so'rash: **I'd like** + ot = «...olmoqchi edim», «...bering, iltimos». «I want» dan ko'ra muloyim.

sentences.text: **I'd like** a coffee with milk, please.
sentences.translation: Sutli qahva **olmoqchi edim**.

sentences.text: Good morning. **I'd like** two tickets to Bukhara for Friday.
sentences.translation: Xayrli tong. Juma kuniga Buxoroga ikkita chipta **olmoqchi edim**.

sentences.text: We**'d like** a table for four, please.
sentences.translation: To'rt kishilik stol **kerak edi**, iltimos.

sentences.text: Excuse me, **I'd like** the bill, please.
sentences.translation: Kechirasiz, hisobni **olib kelsangiz**.

sentences.text: My son **would like** a cheese sandwich and an orange juice.
sentences.translation: O'g'lim pishloqli buterbrod va apelsin sharbati **xohlaydi**.

sentences.text: **I'd like** this jacket in a bigger size, please.
sentences.translation: Shu kurtkaning kattaroq o'lchamini **xohlardim**.

sentences.text: For dessert Sarah **would like** the chocolate cake.
sentences.translation: Shirinlikka Sara shokoladli tortni **xohlaydi**.

sentences.text: Hi, **I'd like** a kilo of tomatoes and half a kilo of cucumbers.
sentences.translation: Salom, bir kilo pomidor va yarim kilo bodring **olmoqchi edim**.

sentences.text: Tom and I **would like** the same as them.
sentences.translation: Tom ikkalamiz ham xuddi ularnikidek taom **xohlaymiz**.

sentences.text: Good afternoon, **I'd like** a room with a view of the mountains.
sentences.translation: Xayrli kun, tog'lar ko'rinadigan xona **olmoqchi edim**.

examples.title: **I'd like to** ...: wishes and plans
examples.description: **I'd like to** + fe'l = «...ni xohlardim», «...moqchiman»: istak, orzu, rasmiy niyat. Inkor — **wouldn't like to** («...ni xohlamasdim»).

sentences.text: One day **I'd like to** visit London.
sentences.translation: Bir kun Londonga **borishni xohlardim**.

sentences.text: **I'd like to** speak English fluently.
sentences.translation: Inglizchada ravon **gapirishni xohlardim**.

sentences.text: Aziz **would like to** become a pilot.
sentences.translation: Aziz uchuvchi **bo'lishni xohlaydi**.

sentences.text: After university Madina **would like to** work abroad for a few years.
sentences.translation: Universitetdan keyin Madina bir necha yil chet elda **ishlashni xohlaydi**.

sentences.text: We**'d like to** thank you for your help.
sentences.translation: Yordamingiz uchun sizga **rahmat aytmoqchimiz**.

sentences.text: **I'd like to** book an appointment with Dr Karimova, please.
sentences.translation: Doktor Karimovaning qabuliga **yozilmoqchi edim**.

sentences.text: My parents **would like to** meet your family.
sentences.translation: Ota-onam oilangiz bilan **tanishishni xohlaydi**.

sentences.text: Sarah **wouldn't like to** live in a big city — she loves the countryside.
sentences.translation: Sara katta shaharda **yashashni xohlamasdi** — u qishloq joylarni yaxshi ko'radi.

sentences.text: This summer the children **would like to** go to the seaside.
sentences.translation: Bu yoz bolalar dengiz bo'yiga **borishni xohlashadi**.

sentences.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the captain **would like to** welcome you on board.
sentences.translation: Xonimlar va janoblar, kapitan sizni bortda **qutlamoqchi**.

examples.title: **What / Where / When would you like** ...?
examples.description: So'roq so'zli savollar: **What would you like?** — «Nima olasiz?», **Where would you like to go?** — «Qayerga borishni xohlaysiz?». Savol — javob juftliklari.

sentences.text: What **would you like** to drink?
sentences.translation: Nima **ichasiz**?

sentences.text: Where **would you like** to go on holiday this year? — Somewhere warm.
sentences.translation: Bu yil ta'tilga qayerga **borishni xohlaysiz**? — Issiqroq biror joyga.

sentences.text: What time **would you like** to have breakfast? — At eight, please.
sentences.translation: Nonushtani soat nechada **qilishni xohlaysiz**? — Sakkizda, iltimos.

sentences.text: Which room **would you like**, the big one or the small one?
sentences.translation: Qaysi xonani **xohlaysiz**, kattasinimi yoki kichigini?

sentences.text: How **would you like** to pay — by card or in cash?
sentences.translation: Qanday **to'lamoqchisiz** — karta bilanmi yoki naqd?

sentences.text: Who **would you like** to invite to your birthday party?
sentences.translation: Tug'ilgan kuningizga kimni **taklif qilmoqchisiz**?

sentences.text: Bekzod, what **would** you **like** for your birthday? — A new football.
sentences.translation: Bekzod, tug'ilgan kuningga nima **xohlaysan**? — Yangi futbol to'pi.

sentences.text: When **would you like** to start the course? — In September, if possible.
sentences.translation: Kursni qachon **boshlamoqchisiz**? — Iloji bo'lsa, sentyabrda.

sentences.text: How **would you like** your eggs? — Fried, please.
sentences.translation: Tuxumni qanday **pishirib beraylik**? — Qovurilgan bo'lsin, iltimos.

sentences.text: What kind of job **would** Dilnoza **like** after college?
sentences.translation: Kollejdan keyin Dilnoza qanday ish **xohlaydi**?

examples.title: **Do you like** ...? ↔ **Would you like** ...?
examples.description: **Do you like** / **I like** — umuman yoqadi («yaxshi ko'raman»); **Would you like** / **I'd like** — hozir, aniq taklif yoki istak («xohlayman»).

sentences.text: **Do you like** coffee? — Yes, I drink it every morning.
sentences.translation: Qahvani **yaxshi ko'rasizmi**? — Ha, har kuni ertalab ichaman.

sentences.text: **Would you like** a coffee now? — Yes, please, I'm very tired.
sentences.translation: Hozir qahva **ichasizmi**? — Ha, iltimos, juda charchadim.

sentences.text: Aziz **likes** horror films, but tonight he**'d like** to watch a comedy.
sentences.translation: Aziz qo'rqinchli filmlarni **yaxshi ko'radi**, lekin bugun kechqurun komediya **ko'rmoqchi**.

sentences.text: I **like** Samarkand a lot, and **I'd like** to go there again in spring.
sentences.translation: Samarqand menga juda **yoqadi**, bahorda u yerga yana **bormoqchiman**.

sentences.text: **Do** your children **like** swimming? — They love it!
sentences.translation: Bolalaringiz **suzishni yaxshi ko'radimi**? — Juda yaxshi ko'rishadi!

sentences.text: Sarah, **would** you **like** to swim in the lake with us this afternoon?
sentences.translation: Sara, bugun tushdan keyin biz bilan ko'lda **cho'milishni xohlaysanmi**?

sentences.text: Emma doesn't **like** cooking, but she**'d like** to learn how to make plov.
sentences.translation: Emma ovqat pishirishni **yoqtirmaydi**, lekin palov qilishni **o'rganmoqchi**.

sentences.text: We **like** our flat, but one day we**'d like** to have a house with a garden.
sentences.translation: Kvartiramiz bizga **yoqadi**, lekin bir kun bog'li uy **qilishni xohlaymiz**.

sentences.text: **Does** Tom **like** Indian food? — Yes, he loves spicy dishes.
sentences.translation: Tom hind taomlarini **yaxshi ko'radimi**? — Ha, u achchiq taomlarni juda yaxshi ko'radi.

sentences.text: Bekzod, you **like** football — **would** you **like** a ticket to Saturday's match?
sentences.translation: Bekzod, sen futbolni **yaxshi ko'rasan** — shanbadagi o'yinga chipta **xohlaysanmi**?

examples.title: Answers: **Yes, please**, **No, thank you**, **I'd love to**
examples.description: Taklifga javob: **Yes, please.** / **No, thank you.** Chaqiriqqa rozilik — **I'd love to!**, muloyim rad etish — **I'd love to, but ...** («Juda xohlardim, lekin ...»).

sentences.text: Would you like some soup? — **Yes, please.**
sentences.translation: Sho'rva ichasizmi? — **Ha, iltimos.**

sentences.text: More bread? — **No, thank you.** I'm full.
sentences.translation: Yana non? — **Yo'q, rahmat.** To'ydim.

sentences.text: Dilnoza and I are getting married in May. Would you like to come? — **I'd love to!**
sentences.translation: Dilnoza ikkalamiz mayda turmush quryapmiz. Kelasizmi? — **Bajonidil!**

sentences.text: **I'd love to**, but I have to work on Saturday.
sentences.translation: **Juda xohlardim**, lekin shanba kuni ishlashim kerak.

sentences.text: Would Tom like a lift to the station? — **No, thanks**, he**'d like** to walk.
sentences.translation: Tomni vokzalgacha mashinada olib boraylikmi? — **Yo'q, rahmat**, u piyoda **yurmoqchi**.

sentences.text: Can I help you? — Yes, **I'd like** some help with these boxes.
sentences.translation: Yordam beraymi? — Ha, bu qutilarni ko'tarishga **yordam bersangiz yaxshi bo'lardi**.

sentences.text: Another cup of tea, Madina? — **Yes, please**, with lemon this time.
sentences.translation: Yana bir piyola choy, Madina? — **Ha, iltimos**, bu safar limon bilan.

sentences.text: We**'d love to** visit you in Manchester, but we don't have time this year.
sentences.translation: Manchesterga sizni ko'rgani **borishni juda xohlardik**, lekin bu yil vaqtimiz yo'q.

sentences.text: Some cake? — **No, thank you** — I'm on a diet.
sentences.translation: Tort olasizmi? — **Yo'q, rahmat** — men parhezdaman.

sentences.text: Would your sister like to join our English club? — Yes, **she'd love to**.
sentences.translation: Singlingiz ingliz tili klubimizga qo'shilishni xohlaydimi? — Ha, **juda xohlaydi**.

examples.title: Dialogue: in a café
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: kafeda ofitsiant va mijozlar suhbati — **Would you like** ...?, **What would you like** ...?, **I'd like** ..., **Do you like** ...?

sentences.text: — Good evening. **Would you like** a table by the window?
sentences.translation: — Xayrli kech. Deraza yonidagi stolni **xohlaysizmi**?

sentences.text: — Yes, please. We**'d like** a table for two.
sentences.translation: — Ha, iltimos. Ikki kishilik stol **kerak edi**.

sentences.text: — Here's the menu. What **would you like** to drink?
sentences.translation: — Mana menyu. Nima **ichasizlar**?

sentences.text: — **I'd like** a lemonade, and my friend **would like** green tea.
sentences.translation: — Men limonad **xohlardim**, do'stim esa ko'k choy **xohlaydi**.

sentences.text: — Of course. And **would you like** to order food now?
sentences.translation: — Albatta. Taomga ham hozir **buyurtma berasizlarmi**?

sentences.text: — Not yet. **Do you like** spicy food, Tom?
sentences.translation: — Hali emas. Tom, achchiq taomlarni **yaxshi ko'rasanmi**?

sentences.text: — Yes, I love it. The lamb curry, please — **I'd like** to try it.
sentences.translation: — Ha, juda yaxshi ko'raman. Qo'y go'shtidan kari, iltimos — uni **tatib ko'rmoqchiman**.

sentences.text: — Excellent choice. **Would** you **like** some rice with it?
sentences.translation: — Ajoyib tanlov. Yoniga guruch ham **qo'shaylikmi**?

sentences.text: — Yes, please. And **I'd like** some bread too.
sentences.translation: — Ha, iltimos. Non ham **bo'lsin**.

sentences.text: — Certainly. **Would you like** anything else? — No, that's all, thank you.
sentences.translation: — Albatta. Yana biror narsa **xohlaysizmi**? — Yo'q, shu yetarli, rahmat.
